transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, could you tell me what's been bringing you in, or what's been troubling you lately?

I keep getting stuck on this tiny uneven spot around my nose and cheek. I notice it a lot in photos and under the lights at the store. Other people tell me they can’t see it, but it feels like it’s the first thing customers or my managers notice when they look at me.
On a typical day, about how much time would you say you spend thinking about this spot on your face or checking/covering it up?

A lot of my breaks, honestly. I’ll go check it in the bathroom mirror, try to fix my hair around it, and compare myself to girls coming through my line. Sometimes I take so long I’m late getting back to the register.
Aside from checking or fixing this spot on your face, do you find yourself doing similar repeated checking, counting, or ritual-like behaviors about things unrelated to your appearance?
No, I don’t think so. It’s mostly just about my face.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient demonstrates preoccupation with a minor/nonexistent facial flaw (uneven spot near nose/cheek) that others report is not noticeable, indicating a marked discrepancy between perceived and actual appearance. This preoccupation consumes significant time (repeated mirror checking, camouflaging with hair, comparing self to others) and causes functional impairment (being late returning to work). Repetitive behaviors are specifically appearance-focused rather than generalized, ruling out OCD. No evidence of other body-image distortions typical of eating disorders. Diagnosis meets criteria for Body Dysmorphic Disorder (F45.22).
